title: षोडशोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Krishna tells the story of Jarasandha's birth. King Brihadratha of Magadha, childless, received a mango from the sage Chandakaushika and gave half to each of his two queens, who each bore half a child; the halves were thrown out, and a Rakshasi named Jara joined them into a whole, living boy.
summary.kn: ಜರಾಸಂಧನ ಜನ್ಮಕಥೆಯನ್ನು ಶ್ರೀಕೃಷ್ಣನು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಸಂತಾನಹೀನ ಮಗಧರಾಜ ಬೃಹದ್ರಥನು ಚಂಡಕೌಶಿಕ ಋಷಿಯಿಂದ ಮಾವಿನಹಣ್ಣು ಪಡೆದು ಇಬ್ಬರು ರಾಣಿಯರಿಗೆ ಅರ್ಧ ಅರ್ಧ ಕೊಟ್ಟನು; ಒಬ್ಬೊಬ್ಬರೂ ಅರ್ಧ ಶಿಶುವನ್ನು ಹೆತ್ತರು; ಹೊರಗೆಸೆದ ತುಂಡುಗಳನ್ನು ಜರೆ ಎಂಬ ರಾಕ್ಷಸಿ ಜೋಡಿಸಿ ಜೀವಂತ ಬಾಲಕನನ್ನಾಗಿಸಿದಳು.
summary.hi: श्रीकृष्ण जरासन्ध के जन्म की कथा सुनाते हैं। निःसन्तान मगधराज बृहद्रथ ने ऋषि चण्डकौशिक से एक आम पाया और दोनों रानियों को आधा-आधा दिया, जिन्होंने आधा-आधा शिशु जन्मा; टुकड़े बाहर फेंके गए, और जरा नामक राक्षसी ने उन्हें जोड़कर जीवित बालक बना दिया।
summary.te: జరాసంధుని జన్మకథను శ్రీకృష్ణుడు చెబుతాడు. సంతానం లేని మగధరాజు బృహద్రథుడు చండకౌశిక ఋషి నుండి మామిడిపండు పొంది ఇద్దరు రాణులకు సగం సగం ఇచ్చాడు; ఒక్కొక్కరు సగం శిశువును కన్నారు; బయట పారవేసిన ముక్కలను జర అనే రాక్షసి కలిపి జీవించే బాలునిగా చేసింది.
summary.ta: ஜராஸந்தனின் பிறப்புக் கதையை ஸ்ரீகிருஷ்ணர் சொல்கிறார். மக்கட்பேறில்லாத மகத மன்னன் ப்ருஹத்ரதன் சண்டகௌஶிக முனிவரிடம் ஒரு மாம்பழம் பெற்று இரு அரசியருக்கும் பாதி பாதியாகக் கொடுத்தான்; ஒவ்வொருத்தியும் பாதிக் குழந்தையைப் பெற்றாள்; வெளியே எறியப்பட்ட பாதிகளை ஜரா என்ற அரக்கி இணைத்து உயிருள்ள சிறுவனாக்கினாள்.
summary.ml: ജരാസന്ധന്റെ ജനനകഥ കൃഷ്ണൻ പറയുന്നു. മഗധത്തിലെ ബൃഹദ്രഥരാജാവ് പുത്രന്മാരില്ലാതിരുന്നപ്പോൾ ചണ്ഡകൗശികൻ ഋഷിയിൽ നിന്ന് ഒരു മാമ്പഴം ലഭിക്കുന്നു; അദ്ദേഹം അത് രണ്ടു റാണിമാർക്കും പകുതി വീതം നൽകുന്നു, ഓരോരുത്തരും ഓരോ പകുതി കുഞ്ഞിനെ പ്രസവിക്കുന്നു. ആ പകുതികൾ വെളിയിലെറിയപ്പെടുന്നു; ജര എന്ന രാക്ഷസി അവയെ ചേർത്ത് ജീവനുള്ള ഒരു ആൺകുട്ടിയാക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 2.16; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Apr 19 2006

verses.text: वासुदेव उवाच

meaning.en: Vasudeva said:

verses.text:
जातस्य भारते वंशे तथा कुन्त्याः सुतस्य च ।
या वै युक्ता मतिः सेयमर्जुनेन प्रदर्शिता ॥

meaning.en: This resolve that Arjuna has shown is just what suits one born in the Bharata line and a son of Kunti.

verses.text:
न मृत्योः समयं विद्म रात्रौ वा यदि वा दिवा ।
न चापि कंचिदमरमयुद्धेनापि शुश्रुमः ॥

meaning.en: We do not know the hour of death, whether by night or day, nor have we heard of anyone who became immortal by not fighting.

verses.text:
एतावदेव पुरुषैः कार्यं हृदयतोषणम् ।
नयेन विधिदृष्टेन यदुपक्रमते परान् ॥

meaning.en: This much is a man's task, to please the heart: to move against his enemies by policy as the rule shows.

verses.text:
सुनयस्यानपायस्य संयुगे परमः क्रमः ।
संशयो जायते साम्ये साम्यं च न भवेद्द्वयोः ॥

meaning.en: For one of good policy who suffers no loss, the best course in battle is clear; doubt arises among equals, and no two are ever truly equal.

verses.text:
ते वयं नयमास्थाय शत्रुदेहसमीपगाः ।
कथमन्तं न गच्छेम वृक्षस्येव नदीरयाः ।
पररन्ध्रे पराक्रान्ताः स्वरन्ध्रावरणे स्थिताः ॥

meaning.en: So, resting on policy and going near our enemy's person, why should we not reach the end, as river currents reach a tree's root? Attacking the enemy's weak point, we stay behind a cover over our own.

verses.text:
व्यूढानीकैरनुबलैर्नोपेयाद्बलवत्तरम् ।
इति बुद्धिमतां नीतिस्तन्ममापीह रोचते ॥

meaning.en: One should not approach a stronger foe with massed troops and followers; this is the policy of the wise, and it pleases me here too.

verses.text:
अनवद्या ह्यसंबुद्धाः प्रविष्टाः शत्रुसद्म तत् ।
शत्रुदेहमुपाक्रम्य तं कामं प्राप्नुयामहे ॥

meaning.en: Blameless and unannounced, we will enter that enemy's house, and, closing on his person, we shall get what we want.

verses.text:
एको ह्येव श्रियं नित्यं बिभर्ति पुरुषर्षभ ।
अन्तरात्मेव भूतानां तत्क्षये वै बलक्षयः ॥

meaning.en: One man alone always bears the fortune, like the inner self of beings; when he is gone, the strength is gone.

verses.text:
अथ चेत्तं निहत्याजौ शेषेणाभिसमागताः ।
प्राप्नुयाम ततः स्वर्गं ज्ञातित्राणपरायणाः ॥

meaning.en: And if we kill him in battle and return with the rest alive, devoted to saving our kin, we shall win heaven.

verses.text: युधिष्ठिर उवाच

meaning.en: Yudhishthira said:

verses.text:
कृष्ण कोऽयं जरासंधः किंवीर्यः किंपराक्रमः ।
यस्त्वां स्पृष्ट्वाग्निसदृशं न दग्धः शलभो यथा ॥

meaning.en: Krishna, who is this Jarasandha, what is his strength and what his courage, that he touched you, who are like fire, and was not burned, like a moth?

verses.text: कृष्ण उवाच

meaning.en: Krishna said:

verses.text:
शृणु राजञ्जरासंधो यद्वीर्यो यत्पराक्रमः ।
यथा चोपेक्षितोऽस्माभिर्बहुशः कृतविप्रियः ॥

meaning.en: Hear, O king, of Jarasandha's strength and courage, and how he did us many wrongs, though we overlooked them.

verses.text:
अक्षौहिणीनां तिसृणामासीत्समरदर्पितः ।
राजा बृहद्रथो नाम मगधाधिपतिः पतिः ॥

meaning.en: There was a king named Brihadratha, lord of Magadha, proud in war, with three akshauhinis.

verses.text:
रूपवान्वीर्यसंपन्नः श्रीमानतुलविक्रमः ।
नित्यं दीक्षाकृशतनुः शतक्रतुरिवापरः ॥

meaning.en: He was handsome, strong, splendid and of matchless prowess, his body thin from continual vows of consecration, like a second Shatakratu.

verses.text:
तेजसा सूर्यसदृशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः ।
यमान्तकसमः कोपे श्रिया वैश्रवणोपमः ॥

meaning.en: He was like the sun in brilliance, like the earth in patience, like Yama the ender in anger, and like Vaishravana in wealth.

verses.text:
तस्याभिजनसंयुक्तैर्गुणैर्भरतसत्तम ।
व्याप्तेयं पृथिवी सर्वा सूर्यस्येव गभस्तिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Best of the Bharatas, the whole earth was filled with the virtues of his lineage, as with the sun's rays.

verses.text:
स काशिराजस्य सुते यमजे भरतर्षभ ।
उपयेमे महावीर्यो रूपद्रविणसंमते ॥

meaning.en: That mighty king married the twin daughters of the king of Kashi, who were honored for their beauty and wealth.

verses.text:
तयोश्चकार समयं मिथः स पुरुषर्षभः ।
नातिवर्तिष्य इत्येवं पत्नीभ्यां संनिधौ तदा ॥

meaning.en: The best of men made a pact with them in private, in the presence of both wives, that he would not go beyond them.

verses.text:
स ताभ्यां शुशुभे राजा पत्नीभ्यां मनुजाधिप ।
प्रियाभ्यामनुरूपाभ्यां करेणुभ्यामिव द्विपः ॥

meaning.en: The king shone with those two fitting and beloved wives, as an elephant bull with two cow elephants, O lord of men.

verses.text:
तयोर्मध्यगतश्चापि रराज वसुधाधिपः ।
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये मूर्तिमानिव सागरः ॥

meaning.en: The ruler of the earth, standing between the two, looked like the ocean in bodily form between the Ganga and the Yamuna.

verses.text:
विषयेषु निमग्नस्य तस्य यौवनमत्यगात् ।
न च वंशकरः पुत्रस्तस्याजायत कश्चन ॥

meaning.en: Sunk in pleasures, his youth passed, and no son was born to him to continue the line.

verses.text:
मङ्गलैर्बहुभिर्होमैः पुत्रकामाभिरिष्टिभिः ।
नाससाद नृपश्रेष्ठः पुत्रं कुलविवर्धनम् ॥

meaning.en: With many auspicious acts, fire offerings and sacrifices for a son, the best of kings did not obtain a son to increase his family.

verses.text:
अथ काक्षीवतः पुत्रं गौतमस्य महात्मनः ।
शुश्राव तपसि श्रान्तमुदारं चण्डकौशिकम् ॥

meaning.en: Then he heard that Chandakaushika, noble son of Kakshivat, the great Gautama, was weary from austerities.

verses.text:
यदृच्छयागतं तं तु वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितम् ।
पत्नीभ्यां सहितो राजा सर्वरत्नैरतोषयत् ॥

meaning.en: The sage had come by chance and was resting at the foot of a tree; the king, with his two wives, satisfied him with every kind of jewel.

verses.text:
तमब्रवीत्सत्यधृतिः सत्यवागृषिसत्तमः ।
परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते राजन्वरं वरय सुव्रत ॥

meaning.en: The best of seers, firm in truth and true in speech, said to him, "I am pleased with you, king; ask a boon, you of good vows."

verses.text:
ततः सभार्यः प्रणतस्तमुवाच बृहद्रथः ।
पुत्रदर्शननैराश्याद्बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा ॥

meaning.en: Then Brihadratha, with his wife, bowed to him and said, in a voice choked with tears for despair of seeing a son,

verses.text: बृहद्रथ उवाच

meaning.en: Brihadratha said:

verses.text:
भगवन्राज्यमुत्सृज्य प्रस्थितस्य तपोवनम् ।
किं वरेणाल्पभाग्यस्य किं राज्येनाप्रजस्य मे ॥

meaning.en: Blessed one, I am about to give up the kingdom and go to the forest of austerity; what is a boon to one of poor fortune, what is a kingdom to one without children?

verses.text: कृष्ण उवाच

meaning.en: Krishna said:

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा मुनिर्ध्यानमगमत्क्षुभितेन्द्रियः ।
तस्यैव चाम्रवृक्षस्य छायायां समुपाविशत् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing this, the sage, his senses stirred, went into meditation, and sat in the shade of that very mango tree.

verses.text:
तस्योपविष्टस्य मुनेरुत्सङ्गे निपपात ह ।
अवातमशुकादष्टमेकमाम्रफलं किल ॥

meaning.en: As the sage sat there, a single mango, neither shaken by wind nor bitten by a parrot, fell into his lap.

verses.text:
तत्प्रगृह्य मुनिश्रेष्ठो हृदयेनाभिमन्त्र्य च ।
राज्ञे ददावप्रतिमं पुत्रसंप्राप्तिकारकम् ॥

meaning.en: The best of sages took it, consecrated it in his heart, and gave it to the king, a fruit without equal that brings the birth of a son.

verses.text:
उवाच च महाप्राज्ञस्तं राजानं महामुनिः ।
गच्छ राजन्कृतार्थोऽसि निवर्त मनुजाधिप ॥

meaning.en: The very wise great sage said to the king, "Go, king, your purpose is fulfilled; turn back, lord of men."

verses.text:
यथासमयमाज्ञाय तदा स नृपसत्तमः ।
द्वाभ्यामेकं फलं प्रादात्पत्नीभ्यां भरतर्षभ ॥

meaning.en: Knowing what was fitting, the best of kings then gave the one fruit to his two wives, Bharata.

verses.text:
ते तदाम्रं द्विधा कृत्वा भक्षयामासतुः शुभे ।
भावित्वादपि चार्थस्य सत्यवाक्यात्तथा मुनेः ॥

meaning.en: The two good women cut that mango in two and ate it, both because it was bound to come to pass and because of the sage's true word.

verses.text:
तयोः समभवद्गर्भः फलप्राशनसंभवः ।
ते च दृष्ट्वा नरपतिः परां मुदमवाप ह ॥

meaning.en: From eating the fruit both conceived, and the king, seeing it, was filled with great joy.

verses.text:
अथ काले महाप्राज्ञ यथासमयमागते ।
प्रजायेतामुभे राजञ्शरीरशकले तदा ॥

meaning.en: When the time had come, O wise one, both of them gave birth, each to a piece of a body.

verses.text:
एकाक्षिबाहुचरणे अर्धोदरमुखस्फिजे ।
दृष्ट्वा शरीरशकले प्रवेपाते उभे भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: Each had one eye, one arm, one leg, half a belly, half a face and half a hip; seeing those pieces of body, they both trembled greatly.

verses.text:
उद्विग्ने सह संमन्त्र्य ते भगिन्यौ तदाबले ।
सजीवे प्राणिशकले तत्यजाते सुदुःखिते ॥

meaning.en: The two sisters, helpless and terrified, took counsel together and, in deep grief, abandoned the two living pieces.

verses.text:
तयोर्धात्र्यौ सुसंवीते कृत्वा ते गर्भसंप्लवे ।
निर्गम्यान्तःपुरद्वारात्समुत्सृज्याशु जग्मतुः ॥

meaning.en: Their two nurses wrapped them well in cloths, went out through the gate of the women's quarters, threw them away quickly, and went off.

verses.text:
ते चतुष्पथनिक्षिप्ते जरा नामाथ राक्षसी ।
जग्राह मनुजव्याघ्र मांसशोणितभोजना ॥

meaning.en: As they lay at the crossroads, a female Rakshasa named Jara, who ate flesh and blood, took them up, tiger among men.

verses.text:
कर्तुकामा सुखवहे शकले सा तु राक्षसी ।
संघट्टयामास तदा विधानबलचोदिता ॥

meaning.en: Wishing to make the two pieces easy to carry, the Rakshasa, impelled by fate's power, pressed them together.

verses.text:
ते समानीतमात्रे तु शकले पुरुषर्षभ ।
एकमूर्तिकृते वीरः कुमारः समपद्यत ॥

meaning.en: The moment the two pieces were brought together, tiger among men, a boy of heroic strength came to be, made one in form.

verses.text:
ततः सा राक्षसी राजन्विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचना ।
न शशाक समुद्वोढुं वज्रसारमयं शिशुम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the Rakshasa, her eyes wide with wonder, could not lift the child, whose body was as hard as a thunderbolt.

verses.text:
बालस्ताम्रतलं मुष्टिं कृत्वा चास्ये निधाय सः ।
प्राक्रोशदतिसंरम्भात्सतोय इव तोयदः ॥

meaning.en: The baby, making a fist of his copper-red palm and putting it in his mouth, cried out furiously, like a cloud heavy with water.

verses.text:
तेन शब्देन संभ्रान्तः सहसान्तःपुरे जनः ।
निर्जगाम नरव्याघ्र राज्ञा सह परंतप ॥

meaning.en: At that noise the people in the women's quarters were suddenly startled, and came out with the king, tiger among men, scorcher of foes.

verses.text:
ते चाबले परिग्लाने पयःपूर्णपयोधरे ।
निराशे पुत्रलाभाय सहसैवाभ्यगच्छताम् ॥

meaning.en: The two wives, weak and wasted, their breasts full of milk, hopeless of getting a son, came forward suddenly.

verses.text:
अथ दृष्ट्वा तथाभूते राजानं चेष्टसंततिम् ।
तं च बालं सुबलिनं चिन्तयामास राक्षसी ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the king so, and his hoped-for line, and that strong child, the Rakshasa thought:

verses.text:
नार्हामि विषये राज्ञो वसन्ती पुत्रगृद्धिनः ।
बालं पुत्रमुपादातुं मेघलेखेव भास्करम् ॥

meaning.en: "I should not take a son from the king's land, where I have lived while he longs for a son, as a streak of cloud cannot take hold of the sun."

verses.text:
सा कृत्वा मानुषं रूपमुवाच मनुजाधिपम् ।
बृहद्रथ सुतस्तेऽयं मद्दत्तः प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥

meaning.en: Taking human form, she said to the king, "Brihadratha, take this son of yours, given by me.

verses.text:
तव पत्नीद्वये जातो द्विजातिवरशासनात् ।
धात्रीजनपरित्यक्तो मयायं परिरक्षितः ॥

meaning.en: "He was born to your two wives at the command of the best of Brahmins, cast away by the nurses, and kept safe by me."

verses.text:
ततस्ते भरतश्रेष्ठ काशिराजसुते शुभे ।
तं बालमभिपत्याशु प्रस्नवैरभिषिञ्चताम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the two lovely daughters of the king of Kashi, best of the Bharatas, hastened to the baby and bathed him with their milk.

verses.text:
ततः स राजा संहृष्टः सर्वं तदुपलभ्य च ।
अपृच्छन्नवहेमाभां राक्षसीं तामराक्षसीम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the king, delighted and having understood everything, asked the Rakshasa, who now looked no Rakshasa, with the glow of fresh gold.

verses.text:
का त्वं कमलगर्भाभे मम पुत्रप्रदायिनी ।
कामया ब्रूहि कल्याणि देवता प्रतिभासि मे ॥

meaning.en: "Who are you, with a lotus-womb's radiance, who give me a son? Tell me what you wish, lovely one; you seem a goddess to me."
